assertion.statement: For the actual local cyclotomic tower at2 and fixed Tate-module twist, rational H2_Iw/(gamma-1) identifies with H2(Q2,V chi). The local Iwasawa complex has no cohomology above degree2 under the stated finite-cohomology hypotheses.
assertion.objects: The fixed rank-two integral Tate module T chi over G_Q2 and the local cyclotomic Z2 extension; V=T tensor Q2.
assertion.hypotheses: The finite local Galois cohomology theorem gives cd2(G_Q2)=2 and finite cohomology for finite2-primary coefficients. T chi is finite free over Z2 with continuous action. The same convention of corestriction and inverse cyclotomic action is used.
assertion.quantifiers: Each of the finitely many fixed local twists and sign components used for F2.
assertion.parameter_range: The nonarchimedean place2; finite twists of the same elliptic Tate module.
assertion.uniformity: One identification for each fixed local type; no numerical bound on characteristic elements.
assertion.constants: No numerical constant or scalar rescaling.
assertion.normalizations: t=gamma-1 at the central character; tensor with Q2 only after the integral descent identity.
assertion.exceptional_cases: This does not prove H2(Q2,V chi)=0, local elliptic torsion finiteness, or the finite list of twisting types. Those are separate inputs to F2(0) nonzero.
assertion.limit_order: Fix the local twist and tower, form Iwasawa cohomology with corestriction, descend by augmentation, and then rationalize.

use.reason: This supplies the derived local-control step used to compare central local H2 with finite-level H2. It does not supply its vanishing.
use.shared_contract_justification: Both occurrences use the identical fixed local Tate twist, cyclotomic tower and central augmentation in the F2 correction argument.

supplier.statement: For an admissible finite-type coefficient complex and a quotient Gamma isomorphic to Z_p, derived Iwasawa cohomology tensored over the Iwasawa algebra with its augmentation is continuous cohomology. If cd_p(G)=e and the complex is concentrated in degrees at most n, the degree e+n Iwasawa coinvariants identify with degree e+n continuous cohomology.

publication.title: Selmer Complexes
publication.corrections: No inverse-limit or real-place conclusion outside the stated admissibility and cohomological-dimension hypotheses.

available_assertion.statement: For an admissible finite-type coefficient complex and a quotient Gamma isomorphic to Z_p, derived Iwasawa cohomology tensored over the Iwasawa algebra with its augmentation is continuous cohomology. If cd_p(G)=e and the complex is concentrated in degrees at most n, the degree e+n Iwasawa coinvariants identify with degree e+n continuous cohomology.
available_assertion.objects: A profinite group G, closed normal H, Gamma=G/H, complete coefficient ring R, and an admissible finite-type R[G] coefficient complex T.
available_assertion.hypotheses: Gamma is Z_p for the one-variable conclusion; T is bounded below and finite-type admissible. The top-degree conclusion assumes cd_p(G)=e finite and T has no terms above n. The separate inverse-limit identification in8.3.5(ii) assumes condition(F).
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every group, coefficient complex and quotient satisfying these hypotheses.
available_assertion.uniformity: Functorial algebraic identification, not a quantitative bound.
available_assertion.normalizations: Augmentation Gamma to1; projective transition maps are corestriction, with the induced coefficient convention of8.3.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: No real-place assertion when p=2 and cd_p is infinite. No vanishing of finite-level H2 follows from this theorem.
available_assertion.limit_order: The source defines derived Iwasawa cohomology before applying derived augmentation; its spectral sequence supplies the top-degree identification.
